name: Selfheal
grown_as: A wild perennial of lawns and meadows.
habit: A low creeping perennial: leafy stems run along the ground and root, sending up short upright flowering stems 5 to 30 cm, each topped with one dense head. In a mown lawn it flowers at only a few centimetres.

leaf.base: Rounded or narrowing to a short wedge
leaf.margin: Smooth or with a few very shallow, wavy teeth
leaf.veins: A midrib and 3 to 5 side veins each side, a little pressed in
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves on stalks 1 to 3 cm; one pair of stalkless leaves sits right under each flower head

flower.form: A small two-lipped flower: a hooded upper lip over a three-lobed lower lip, the middle lobe fringed
flower.petals: Five petals joined into a tube, opening into the two lips
flower.behind: A two-lipped purplish calyx, and under each whorl a broad, rounded, pointed, hairy bract, purple-edged
flower.carried: In a dense, squarish, oblong head 2 to 4 cm long at the top of each stem, the flowers in whorls, only a ring or two open at once, sticking out sideways

fruit: The head turns brown and keeps its shape, like a small cone, the calyces closing over four nutlets each. Seeds oval, brown, about 1.5 to 2 mm, faintly lined.
seedling: Two rounded seed leaves on stalks, then opposite pairs of oval true leaves
winter: A low mat of small oval leaves, often purplish, along the creeping stems.

leaf: oval leaf, smooth or barely toothed
bloom: a dense squarish head of small hooded blue-violet flowers
purplish rounded bracts between the whorls
seedling: first true leaves an opposite pair of ovals
young: a low mat of opposite oval leaves on creeping stems
flower: short upright stems each topped by one dense squarish violet head
a pair of stalkless leaves just under each head
seedhead: brown cone-like heads keeping their shape on short stems
dormant: a low mat of small oval leaves, often purple-tinged

look_alikes: Bugle (Ajuga reptans) has glossy leaves and long runners; its blue flowers sit in whorls up a leafy spike and have no hood. Ground-ivy has kidney-shaped toothed leaves and flowers in the leaf joints. Cut-leaved selfheal (Prunella laciniata) is creamy white with cut leaves.
